name: Isle of Skye
tagline: Scotland's misty island of cliffs and pinnacles
summary: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides, a wild landscape of rock pinnacles, sea cliffs and clear mountain pools. Portree's colourful harbour is the base for driving to the Old Man of Storr, the Quiraing and Neist Point lighthouse.
seasonNote: May to September has the long days; June often has the best weather. Midges bite in summer, so bring repellent. Winter is dark, wet and many places close.
arrival: Drive or bus from Glasgow (about 5 hours) or Inverness (about 3 hours) over the Skye Bridge. Trains reach Kyle of Lochalsh or Mallaig, with a ferry from Mallaig.
gettingAround: A car is almost essential; roads are narrow and single-track with passing places.
cashTip: Cards and tap payments work almost everywhere, even for small amounts; tipping about 10 to 12.5 percent in restaurants is common if service isn't included.
foodTip: Fresh langoustines and scallops, Cullen skink smoked-fish soup and local whisky.
buyTip: Talisker whisky, Harris tweed and Skye pottery.
